newsitem.title: FRANCE: French heap praise on Italian actor Mastroianni.
newsitem.headline: French heap praise on Italian actor Mastroianni.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac called the death of Italian film star Marcello Mastroianni on Thursday "an enormous loss" while tearful fans wept outside the Paris flat where the actor died.

"He was the most French of all Italian actors," said Prime Minister Alain Juppe, saying his blend of seduction, humour and talent made him "an exceptional personality of the second half of the century".

"Marcello Mastroianni became a cinema legend in his own lifetime and it is all French culture which today pays tribute to this exceptional representative of Italy's culture," Culture Minister Philippe Douste-Blazy said.
The actor was "one of the great giants of European cinema" who had worked with top French and Russian directors as well as Italian film-makers, Douste-Blazy said in a statement.
Mastroianni died at his home in the Rue de Seine on Paris's Left Bank.

French and Italian fans gathered outside the building to honour his memory and catch a glimpse of his companion, French actress Catherine Deneuve and their daughter, actress Chiara Mastroianni, as they emerged.
The two women and and French actor Michel Piccoli were at Mastroianni's side when he died, French radio said.
"He was perhaps the greatest European cinema actor of the last 50 years," producer Daniel Toscan du Plantier said.
"He reminds us of Fellini and of all the great things that made post-war Italian cinema, which is also dead," Toscan du Plantier told LCI television.
"He was a wonderful man," said a sobbing Italian woman on the pavement outside his home.
"It really affects me. He was someone who made his mark on the film industry and who made us feel emotions," said a French neighbour.
Mastroianni, a familiar figure in the streets and restaurants of the Left Bank, had been treated for cancer of the pancreas but continued to make films until his final months, French media said.
